text.p: A leading Palestinian negotiator said on Monday he feared Israel's government would act against Palestinians to try to divert attention from lingering aspects of a corruption scandal.

"It is an internal Israeli matter but we think it is dangerous because usually when the Israeli government suffers an internal crisis of corruption charges it resorts to escalation against Palestinians, be it more land confiscation, more settlements or suffocation of closures," Saeb Erekat said.

Israeli prosecutors rejected on Sunday police recommendations that they indict Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi over the short-lived appointment of an attorney-general.

But they decided Netanyahu's political ally Aryeh Deri, already facing corruption charges, should be charged and that the prime minister's director-general, Avigdor Lieberman, should face further investigation.
Nabil Abu Rdainah, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's adviser, agreed the corruption scandal was an Israeli matter.
"The important thing for us (Palestinians) is that the Israeli government implements the agreements we signed and adheres to it," he told Reuters.

In the West Bank on Monday, Israeli troops wounded five Palestinian demonstrators in clashes that erupted when the Israelis sealed off Sourif village and brought in a bulldozer to demolish the home of a resident arrested for involvement in a series of attacks on Israelis, Palestinian sources said.

They said a 16-year-old Palestinian boy was in serious condition with a gunshot wound in his neck. Another person was wounded with live ammunition and three were shot with less lethal rubber bullets, they said.
